open_points.subject: State 0 acceptance after reopening
open_points.text: “State 0 closes again when its question rounds are clear; the owner then accepts it as a whole.” The text also says “None open” but records no renewed whole-state acceptance after reopening.
open_points.question: Has the owner accepted the reopened State 0 as a whole, so later states may treat R0-24 through R0-71 and the revised sections as settled?
options: Record an explicit renewed acceptance
Treat the accepted individual decisions as acceptance of the whole
Keep State 0 open
open_points.default_guess: Keep State 0 open until an explicit renewed whole-state acceptance is recorded.

open_points.subject: Owner sign-in
open_points.text: “Every request on either is authenticated; anything not authenticated is refused” and “No operation of Registry answers an unauthenticated caller,” while “The owner signs in to the owner interface with the owner credential.”
open_points.question: Which unauthenticated action presents and processes owner sign-in, and what observable result or refusal does it produce?
options: Define sign-in as the sole unauthenticated Registry operation
Put authentication in an external component
Allow an unauthenticated sign-in surface that is not considered an operation
open_points.default_guess: Define a narrowly scoped unauthenticated sign-in operation that creates a protected owner session or returns a generic refusal.

open_points.subject: Consumer access to project context
open_points.text: The Consumer services paragraph says PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet and Cabinet Web mirror “Each ... validates a project id and reads its context in the disclosure class its token allows,” but R0-43 says `context` answers only a service allowed `personal_data` and “today PresuPro and Client Portal.”
open_points.question: Do Cabinet and the Cabinet Web mirror read `context`; if so, which concrete projection and disclosure class do they receive?
options: Only PresuPro and Client Portal read `context`
Give Cabinet services `personal_data` context access
Define a separate non-personal projection for Cabinet services
open_points.default_guess: Only PresuPro and Client Portal read `context`; Cabinet services receive no context unless a separate projection is explicitly promised.

open_points.subject: Cabinet Web mirror network path
open_points.text: “The Cabinet Web mirror ... keeps its read only if it receives a token of its own,” but the service API is reachable only inside VM Platform or through the VPS WireGuard channel, and the mirror's location and channel are not named.
open_points.question: Where does the Cabinet Web mirror run, and through which permitted network boundary can it call Registry if it is given a token?
options: It runs inside VM Platform
It runs on the VPS over WireGuard
It is retired and receives no production token
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as retired and give it no production access until its host and channel are explicitly named.

open_points.subject: External AI provider
open_points.text: The text refers to “the agent's AI provider” and “the external AI providers,” but no actor or trust-boundary entry says which system receives agent outputs, which fields cross that boundary, or whether the provider is inside the Agent boundary.
open_points.question: Is the external model provider part of the Agent actor or a separate recipient, and exactly which Registry-derived outputs may cross to it?
options: Treat the provider as part of the Agent boundary
Model it as a separate external recipient
No Registry-derived output may leave VM Agent
open_points.default_guess: Model the provider as a separate external recipient subject to the same no-`personal_data` restriction as the agent.

open_points.subject: VPS migration source classification
open_points.text: “Test instances — any other instance ... Each holds ... no production personal data,” while the VPS is a non-production Registry source whose imported projects include customers, objects and pointers.
open_points.question: Is the legacy VPS instance a test instance forbidden to hold production personal data, or a separate temporary migration-source trust boundary allowed to hold the existing production data?
options: Define the VPS as a legacy migration source distinct from test instances
Treat it as a test instance and require its data to contain no production personal data
Treat it as production until migration completes
open_points.default_guess: Define the VPS as a temporary legacy migration source with an explicit trust boundary, distinct from test instances.

open_points.subject: Agent projection and uninspected text
open_points.text: The agent “never receives a `personal_data` value,” yet room names, `uri`, `payload_ref` and digest stay in its projection, the owner or producer is merely instructed not to put names or addresses in them, and “Registry does not inspect these values.”
open_points.question: What observable validation or trust precondition makes the no-`personal_data` guarantee true when uninspected free-text and references are returned to the agent?
options: Validate and reject unsafe values
Remove these values from the agent projection
State that the guarantee depends on trusted owner and producer compliance
open_points.default_guess: Exclude unconstrained text and references from the agent projection unless their allowed syntax is validated to prevent personal values.

open_points.subject: Anonymised project retaining artifact pointers
open_points.text: “An anonymised project keeps its id, status and artifact pointers,” artifacts are “listed and read as before,” and R0-71 says it “holds no personal value,” although Registry neither inspects pointer values nor reads the referenced payload.
open_points.question: How can anonymisation guarantee that no personal value or re-identifying link remains while preserving readable `uri` and `payload_ref` values and their targets?
options: Remove or redact pointer references during anonymisation
Retain only non-identifying pointer metadata
Make the guarantee conditional on a recorded external assessment
open_points.default_guess: Retain only non-identifying pointer metadata; remove readable external references unless an explicit assessment establishes they cannot re-identify.

open_points.subject: Migration export
open_points.text: “The owner exports the chosen source and uploads the export through the owner interface,” but the primary actions contain import only and no source-export action, output or failure.
open_points.question: What product action produces the export from the VPS or test-rig Registry, who may invoke it, what does it contain, and how does failure appear?
options: Add an authenticated Registry export action
Define export as an administrative store operation outside Registry
Name an existing external export tool and its contract
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner-authenticated export action producing one complete, versioned migration package or a clear refusal.

open_points.subject: Retention-review observations
open_points.text: “Registry gives that review what it needs,” including the project archive date and customer relationship-ended mark, but the declared customer reads omit ended and restricted state and no action identifies records due for review.
open_points.question: Through which declared action can the owner observe archive dates, relationship-ended dates, restriction state and the records to consider during the periodic retention review?
options: Include the facts in existing owner reads and lists
Add a dedicated retention-review view/action
Require the owner to derive them from the audit log
open_points.default_guess: Expose the current retention-relevant facts in owner reads and provide an owner-only review list; do not rely on the erasable audit history.

open_points.subject: Agent-authority checks for session-level operations
open_points.text: R0-53 says “On every agent-authority call Registry checks ... the `project_id` is in that session's set,” but registering a session starts with no granted project, and registering, reading session access and requesting access do not require a granted `project_id`.
open_points.question: Which agent-authority operations are project-scoped and therefore require a granted `project_id`, and which session-level operations are allowed without one?
options: Apply the project check only to project-scoped operations
Require a project for every agent-authority operation
Use a separate authority class for session-level operations
open_points.default_guess: Apply the project-membership check only to project-scoped operations; session registration and access operations require an authenticated Kernel and a valid session as applicable.

open_points.subject: Session access version
open_points.text: “read the session's access” returns “the access version,” but no decision says which grants, revocations, active-project changes, pending requests, request answers, archiving or erasures change that version.
open_points.question: What state does the access version cover, and exactly which accepted actions increment it?
options: Version the entire session-access record
Version only the granted project set
Use separate versions for grants, active project and pending request
open_points.default_guess: Use one monotonic version for every mutation of the session's grants, active project or pending request.

open_points.subject: Revision checks across owner-interface changes
open_points.text: R0-29 says “Every change ... made against an older revision is refused,” while R0-35 gives revisions only to projects and customers, and the owner interface also changes session access, imports and audit entries without any named revision.
open_points.question: Does stale-revision refusal apply only to changes of Project and Customer records, or must session access, imports and audit-log erasure also expose revision inputs?
options: Limit revision checks to Project and Customer changes
Add revisions to every mutable owner-interface resource
Specify separate concurrency guards for non-record actions
open_points.default_guess: Use record revisions for Project and Customer changes and explicitly define separate concurrency or idempotency guards for session, import and audit actions.

open_points.subject: No-duplication data-protection promise
open_points.text: R0-37 says “Data is kept only where a stated purpose needs it and not duplicated,” while consumers snapshot Registry identity and Client Portal keeps a local permitted projection when Registry is unavailable.
open_points.question: Is “not duplicated” limited to duplicate storage inside Registry, or does it prohibit the expressly permitted consumer snapshots and Portal projection?
options: Limit the rule to duplicate copies inside Registry
Allow documented purpose-bound service projections
Prohibit persistent downstream copies
open_points.default_guess: Interpret it as prohibiting unnecessary duplication inside Registry while allowing explicitly contracted, purpose-bound consumer projections.
